classification.difficultyReason: Read how each curve behaves on either side of its horizontal tangent, including the concavity change in the increasing curve.

content.prompt: The diagrams below show three different types of stationary points. Classify them accordingly.

spec.description: Unlabelled U-shaped curve with an arrowhead at each upper end. The source's common blue line has no series distinction and uses house black here.
spec.mathematics: Smooth upward-opening curve with a horizontal tangent at its lowest point. No axes, ticks or point labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Student sees only the curve. Classification is in the answers.

answer.worked: The curve decreases before the stationary point and increases after it, so the stationary point is a minimum turning point.

spec.description: Unlabelled inverted U-shaped curve with an arrowhead at each lower end. The source's common blue line has no series distinction and uses house black here.
spec.mathematics: Smooth downward-opening curve with a horizontal tangent at its highest point. No axes, ticks or point labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Student sees only the curve. Classification is in the answers.

answer.worked: The curve increases before the stationary point and decreases after it, so the stationary point is a maximum turning point.

spec.description: Unlabelled increasing S-shaped curve with arrowheads at the lower-left and upper-right ends. The source's common blue line has no series distinction and uses house black here.
spec.mathematics: Smooth increasing curve with a central horizontal tangent and a change in concavity. No axes, ticks or point labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Student sees only the curve. Classification is in the answers.

answer.worked: The curve increases on both sides of the stationary point and changes concavity there, so the stationary point is a horizontal point of inflection.
